reason: Moses is extensively portrayed as an active national leader throughout this passage. He convenes the elders (19:7: 'וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה וַיִּקְרָא לְזִקְנֵי הָעָם'), serves as intermediary between God and the people (19:3-8, 24:3-4), physically leads the people (19:17: 'וַיּוֹצֵא מֹשֶׁה אֶת־ הָעָם'), makes executive decisions, records the law (24:4), intercedes for the nation during the golden calf crisis (32:30-34), and is explicitly called 'the man' ('הָאִישׁ') who brought Israel from Egypt (32:1, 32:23). His authority is recognized by both God and the people; he mediates disputes and directs the covenant ratification ceremony. He is not aspiring to leadership but actively exercising it.
